top_categories.workout_context: Race-pace efforts that mimic Belgrade Gran Fondo's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before October.
63ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.

Road-specific control matters at Belgrade Gran Fondo. Practice on mixed terrain: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 78 miles.
78 miles on mixed terrain burns energy faster than the distance suggests. Train the fade resistance now.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Belgrade Gran Fondo. Train it until it feels boring.
When someone attacks on mixed terrain, you have 10 seconds to respond or you're off the back. This builds that response.
At Belgrade Gran Fondo, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
Double-threshold training builds sustained power with less fatigue. More FTP per hour of training.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Belgrade Gran Fondo. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 4,921ft of climbing on mixed terrain does to your power file on race day.
Varied gradients on mixed terrain demand climbing versatility. Sit the shallow stuff, stand the steep stuff, switch without thinking.
Base fitness for Belgrade Gran Fondo. Without this, the hard workouts break you down instead of building you up.
